raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## What

Replace the single `model-executor` job with four named jobs that each run whole directories of `tests/model_executor`, keeping `main`'s `-m '(not slow_test)'` filter. Core is the catch-all: it runs `model_executor/` minus the directories the other three jobs own, so new tests run by default.

## Old

```text
model-executor   (H200 MIG 35GB) Model Executor  +  (MI300) mirror with its own commands
  pytest model_executor -m '(not slow_test)'
  pytest entrypoints/openai/completion/test_tensorizer_entrypoint.py
```

## New

| Key (each with an `amd-<key>` MI300 mirror) | Runs (all with `-m '(not slow_test)'`) |
| --- | --- |
| `model-executor-tensorizer` | `model_loader/tensorizer_loader` |
| `model-executor-sharded-state-weights-registry` | `model_loader/sharded_state`, `model_loader/weights`, `model_loader/registry` |
| `model-executor-reload` | `model_loader/reload`, then `entrypoints/openai/completion/test_tensorizer_entrypoint.py` |
| `model-executor-core` | `pytest model_executor --ignore=` the five directories above (catch-all) |

```text
tests/model_executor/
├── test_routed_experts_capture.py, test_sleep_mode_tensor_ownership.py, test_triton_dispatcher.py   <- Core
├── warmup/  mrope/  quantization/  models/  custom_ops/  utils/  layers/  kernels/  offloader/      <- Core
└── model_loader/
    ├── test_model_load_with_params.py, fastsafetensors/instanttensor/runai loaders                  <- Core
    ├── tensorizer_loader/                                                                           <- Tensorizer
    ├── sharded_state/test_sharded_state_loader.py, weights/, registry/                              <- Sharded State, Weights and Registry
    └── reload/test_reload.py                                                                        <- Reload
```

## Notes

- Each MI300 mirror has its own `commands` for its unit (the two exports plus its pytest lines, no `apt-get`), replacing the whole-suite mirror commands from #58607. Triggers are `main`'s list, shared through one anchor per lane.
- The 2-GPU Distributed Models job (NVIDIA, its MI300 mirror, legacy MI300 and Intel) runs `sharded_state/` with `-m 'distributed(num_gpus=2)'`, so tp=1 cases no longer run on both the 1-GPU and 2-GPU lanes. Two ROCm-only test-isolation fixes are included (Gemma hidden-act, NVFP4A16 reload skip).
- Tethering passes with and without legacy `test-amd.yaml`. The legacy MI300 job still runs `pytest model_executor` whole, and every moved path is swept (including the Intel `--deselect`).
- AI assistance was used (Claude Code); the submitter reviewed the diff.

## Expected runtime and overhead

Estimates from build [91124](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91124) (previous head, slow tests on), minus the `slow_test` cases and with the entrypoint file moved. Measurement on this head will follow.

| Job | pytest | running wall | non-pytest overhead | main overhead cause |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Tensorizer | ~16m | ~17.5m | ~1.5m | image pull + `apt-get install` |
| Sharded State, Weights and Registry | ≤14m | ≤15m | ~1m | same |
| Reload | ~9m (reload ~5m + entrypoint ~3.7m) | ~10m | ~1m | same |
| Core | ≤15.7m | ≤17m | ~1m | same |

- Worker-minutes: about 56.8 before (same-day unsharded `main`). After is estimated at 57–60, about +3 (budget 20), because the ~11.6m of slow tests are out again and three extra setups cost about 4m.
- Slowest job ~16m, down from ~57m. Four jobs are needed because the remaining ~50m of pytest does not fit three ~15m jobs.

## Validation

Build: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89006 — scoped to `model-executor` and `distributed-model-tests-2-gpus`, head `c6aef7d725`, all jobs passed.

**Model Executor** (pytest time from the session summaries, wall from job start to finish; setup is ~1m per shard)

| Index | Directories | pytest | wall | predicted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `tensorizer_loader` + entrypoints tensorizer file | 17.1m | 18.3m | 17.5m |
| 1 | `sharded_state` + `weights` + `registry` | 12.7m | 13.8m | 12.7m |
| 2 | `reload` + `params` + `fastsafetensors_loader` + `instanttensor_loader` + `runai_streamer_loader` | **24.1m** | 25.3m | 11.1m |
| 3 | `layers` + `mrope` + `kernels` + `utils` + `models` + `custom_ops` + `warmup` + `quantization` + `moe` + `offloader` + `sleep_mode` | 11.5m | 12.4m | 9.0m + sleep_mode |

**Distributed Models** (2-GPU lane, unchanged parallelism): shards 1–3 ran 10.9m / 6.0m / 12.2m of pytest and passed. The `distributed(num_gpus=2)` selection collected and ran the tp=2 sharded-state case (2 passed, 3 deselected).

Slowest shard **24.1m** vs the 51.7m pre-shard p90 baseline; the body predicted 17.5m.

Where the miss comes from: `test_reload.py` measured **18.6m** against 5.0m in the baseline, because the `slow_test` params the old `-m '(not slow_test)'` filter deselected now run — the DeepSeek-V3 debug variants and the quantized Qwen3 variants at tp=1, roughly 1.4–2.3m each (the tp=2 params skip instantly on one device). That is the cost of closing the hole the body describes, and it was unmeasurable before this build. The other never-run set, the four `sleep_mode` cases, cost 3.5m total, so index 3 landed at 11.5m.

Verdict: layout and routing validated; index 2 misses the 20m per-shard target. Proposed fix, same shard count: `reload` alone on index 2 (18.6m) and `params` + the three loader directories (5.5m) join index 3 (→ 17.0m). Slowest shard becomes 18.6m.

## Validation (second run, final assignment)

Build: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89155 — scoped to `model-executor`, head `a30b23d22c`, all four shards passed.

| Index | Directories | pytest | wall | 89006 (previous assignment) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `tensorizer_loader` + entrypoints tensorizer file | 14.7m | 16.4m | 17.1m |
| 1 | `sharded_state` + `weights` + `registry` | 11.7m | 13.0m | 12.7m |
| 2 | `reload` | 14.3m | 15.5m | 24.1m (with params + loaders) |
| 3 | `layers` … `sleep_mode` + `params` + three loader dirs | 15.1m | 18.6m | 11.5m (without params + loaders) |

Slowest shard **15.1m** of pytest vs the 51.7m pre-shard p90 baseline; the body's prediction for the rebalance was 18.6m. Every shard is under the 20m target with headroom, so `timeout_in_minutes: 30` holds.

Two test-ordering bugs surfaced by the regrouping are fixed in this head and confirmed here: the three `test_model_load_with_params` cases (offline-mode flag leaked from `utils/test_weight_utils.py`) and `test_runai_safetensors_weights_iterator_clones_reused_buffers` (default torch device leaked from `quantization/test_eagle_quantization.py`) all pass. `test_qwen3_omni::test_dspark_shares_target_embedding_with_smaller_draft_vocabulary`, which was failing on `main` (builds 89112, 89113) and in the two earlier runs here, passed on this head.

Verdict: layout, routing and shard assignment validated; ready for review.

## Validation — build [#90477](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90477) (four named jobs)

Commit `6be31be05b` (`refs/pull/56890/head`, on latest `main`). Scoped to `model-executor-{tensorizer,sharded-state-weights-registry,reload,core}`, `distributed-model-tests-2-gpus`, and the `amd-` mirror of each.

**Result: primary lane all green; mirror lane 2 of 4 Model Executor jobs failed.** Both failures are ROCm-only test bugs that the restructure exposed, fixed in `cd03774df6` (see below). All 2-GPU Distributed Models shards passed on both lanes.

### Primary lane, measured (`pytest | running wall | non-pytest overhead | main overhead cause`)

| job | pytest | wall | overhead | cause | 89155 (case-routing index) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: |
| Model Executor / Tensorizer | 18.3m | 20.1m | 1.8m | checkout + container start | 14.7m |
| Model Executor / Sharded State, Weights and Registry | 16.1m | 17.3m | 1.2m | checkout + container start | 11.7m |
| Model Executor / Reload | 16.1m | 17.3m | 1.2m | checkout + container start | 14.3m |
| Model Executor / Core | 16.0m | 17.1m | 1.1m | checkout + container start | 15.1m |

- Baseline, same-day unsharded `main` (builds 90473 / 90455): 54.9 / 53.9m pytest, 56.8 / 56.2m wall.
- Total worker-minutes 56.8 → 71.8, **+15.0 extra (budget ≤ 20: pass)**. Of that, +11.6m is pytest: the `slow_test` cases that `-m '(not slow_test)'` used to drop now run. Only +3.4m is repeated setup.
- Slowest job 18.3m pytest / 20.1m wall (**budget ≤ 20m pytest: pass**), down from ~55m for the single job.
- Each job's pytest time is higher than the 89155 forecast, for the same reason: this head no longer deselects `slow_test`.

### Mirror lane

Tensorizer and Sharded State/Weights/Registry passed, both well inside the timeout. The other two failed:

- **Core, 6 failures:** every case of `models/test_gemma_hidden_act.py::test_gemma_mlp_supports_hidden_act_variants`, with `NotImplementedError: Could not run 'vllm::rocm_unquantized_gemm' with arguments from the 'CPU' backend`. The test builds its MLP on the default device. In the old single job it only passed because `test_eagle_quantization.py` ran earlier and leaked a CUDA default device, which this PR fixes. **Fix:** build the MLP on `current_platform.device_type` explicitly.
- **Reload, 1 failure:** `test_reload_weights[...DeepSeek-V3-debug-empty-NVFP4A16...-1]`, with `Forced NVFP4 kernel MarlinNvFp4LinearKernel is not supported: Marlin FP4 not available`. This is a `slow_test` case that `main` never ran. **Fix:** skip it when `is_fp4_marlin_supported()` is false, the same way the FP8 cases already skip.

### Still to run

- Rerun the two failed mirror jobs on `cd03774df6`.
- A legacy `amd-ci` build for `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml`. It needs a maintainer's `/amd-ci run` or the `ready` label.

## Validation rerun — build [#90502](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90502)

Commit `cd03774df6` (`refs/pull/56890/head`, on latest `main`). Scoped to the two jobs the fix touches, on both lanes: `model-executor-core`, `model-executor-reload`, `amd-model-executor-core`, `amd-model-executor-reload`. **All four passed on the first attempt.**

- **Mirror lane, Core:** 619 passed, 30 skipped. The 6 `test_gemma_mlp_supports_hidden_act_variants` cases that failed in #90477 now pass (613 → 619 passed).
- **Mirror lane, Reload:** 52 passed, 11 skipped. The NVFP4A16 reload case now skips instead of failing, because Marlin FP4 is unavailable on that lane.
- **Primary lane:** still green after the fix, and the Gemma test now runs on the accelerator there too.

| job (primary lane) | pytest | running wall | non-pytest overhead | main overhead cause |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Model Executor / Core | 14.7m | 16.2m | 1.5m | checkout + container start |
| Model Executor / Reload | 13.7m | 14.9m | 1.2m | checkout + container start |

These timings combine this build's Core and Reload with Tensorizer and Sharded State/Weights/Registry from #90477:

- **Primary lane:** 56.8 → 68.5 worker-minutes, **+11.7 extra (≤ 20: pass)**. Slowest job 18.3m pytest (Tensorizer; **≤ 20m: pass**).
- **Mirror lane:** every job passed, the slowest well inside its timeout and far below the unsharded baseline. Extra worker-minutes are also within the 20-minute budget.

Still to run: the legacy `amd-ci` build for `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml`. It needs a maintainer's `/amd-ci run` or the `ready` label.

## Validation (rebased head `8036da893c`)

Build: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91124 — diff-selected, same environment as `/ci run`. The PR was rebased onto current `main`; the only follow-up is moving main's new `model_loader/test_mm_encoder_only_weight_filter.py` into `model_loader/weights/`, so it is claimed by the Sharded State, Weights and Registry job.

**All 14 jobs this PR touches passed**: the four Model Executor named jobs and their four mirrors, plus the three 2-GPU Distributed Models shards on each lane. The build's single failure is an unrelated FusedMoE Layer Kernels job that hung in `kernels/moe/test_moe_layer.py` (deepep low-latency case) and timed out. That job passed on a same-day `main` build.

| Job | primary pytest / wall (min) | mirror pytest / wall (min) |
|---|---|---|
| Model Executor / Tensorizer | 19.5 / 21.3 | 16.0 / 18.1 |
| Model Executor / Sharded State, Weights and Registry | 14.0 / 15.0 | 13.1 / 15.4 |
| Model Executor / Reload | 13.8 / 14.9 | 10.5 / 12.9 |
| Model Executor / Core | 15.7 / 16.8 | 9.2 / 11.6 |

Non-pytest overhead is 1–2 min per job on the primary lane and 2–2.5 min on the mirror; that is the image pull plus `apt-get install`.

- Primary lane: unsplit baseline 56.8 worker-min, now 68.0, so **+11.2 extra** (budget 20: pass). The previous run measured +11.7, and most of the extra is the `slow_test` cases that now run. Slowest pytest is 19.5 min (Tensorizer), under the 20 min target (it measured 18.3 on the previous run).
- Mirror lane: unsplit baseline 50.2–55.2 worker-min, now 58.0, so **+2.8 to +7.8 extra** (pass). Slowest pytest is 16.0 min.
- The legacy `amd-ci` pipeline has not run yet; `test-amd.yaml` changes only `source_file_dependencies` paths.

Thanks @khluu, all five done in a17fef83ef (rebased onto current `main`):

- **Tensorizer:** `test_tensorizer_entrypoint.py` moved to the Reload job.
- **`slow_test`:** `-m '(not slow_test)'` is back on all four jobs and their mirrors.
- **Core catch-all:** `test_reload.py` moved to `model_loader/reload/` and `test_sharded_state_loader.py` to `model_loader/sharded_state/`, so every other job runs directories. Core is now `pytest model_executor -m '(not slow_test)' --ignore=` those five directories, and it picks up `test_triton_dispatcher.py`. Every reference to the moved paths is updated: models_distributed, legacy MI300, Intel, and the Intel `--deselect`.
- **Mirrors:** each MI300 mirror has its own `commands` for its unit (the two exports plus its pytest lines, no `apt-get`), so none of them reruns the whole suite. Mirror timeouts dropped to 40.
- **Intel marker:** now `-m "distributed(num_gpus=2)"`, without backslashes.

Tethering passes with and without `test-amd.yaml`. This head still needs its build and `/amd-ci run`. The body has estimates until the build reports.

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @Thangnguyenvn98.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

Closing in favor of automatic runtime sharding: CI now plans each step's shards when the pipeline is generated, from main's per-file timings (`automatic_shard: true`), so hand-split jobs are no longer the approach. `model-executor` is sharded automatically on main (#61202); its AMD mirror is in #61904.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

_(Claude Code here, reviewing on @khluu's behalf.)_

The test moves and the ROCm fixes look good. The job layout needs another pass:
- Tensorizer is 21.3m. Move `test_tensorizer_entrypoint.py` (~3.7m) out, e.g. into Reload.
- `-m 'not slow_test'` got dropped, so ~11.6m of slow tests now run on every PR. Please put it back. Turning on slow tests should be its own PR.
- Core is a hand-picked list and already misses main's new `tests/model_executor/test_triton_dispatcher.py`. Make it a catch-all (`pytest model_executor --ignore=<what the other 3 jobs run>`) or move the root files into subdirs.
- The rebase isn't mechanical. #58607 added `mirror.amd.commands` to the old job, and a clean merge attaches them to the AMD Core mirror, so MI300 would rerun the whole suite. Each mirror needs its own commands (without the apt-get line).
- Intel marker in `models_distributed_intel.yaml`: it should be `-m "distributed(num_gpus=2)"` without the backslashes.

Then a fresh build, plus `/amd-ci run` for the test-amd.yaml changes.

🚀

## Validation

Build: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89006 — scoped to `model-executor` and `distributed-model-tests-2-gpus`, head `c6aef7d725`, all jobs passed.

**Model Executor** (pytest time from the session summaries, wall from job start to finish; setup is ~1m per shard)

| Index | Directories | pytest | wall | predicted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `tensorizer_loader` + entrypoints tensorizer file | 17.1m | 18.3m | 17.5m |
| 1 | `sharded_state` + `weights` + `registry` | 12.7m | 13.8m | 12.7m |
| 2 | `reload` + `params` + `fastsafetensors_loader` + `instanttensor_loader` + `runai_streamer_loader` | **24.1m** | 25.3m | 11.1m |
| 3 | `layers` + `mrope` + `kernels` + `utils` + `models` + `custom_ops` + `warmup` + `quantization` + `moe` + `offloader` + `sleep_mode` | 11.5m | 12.4m | 9.0m + sleep_mode |

**Distributed Models** (2-GPU lane, unchanged parallelism): shards 1–3 ran 10.9m / 6.0m / 12.2m of pytest and passed. The `distributed(num_gpus=2)` selection collected and ran the tp=2 sharded-state case (2 passed, 3 deselected).

Slowest shard **24.1m** vs the 51.7m pre-shard p90 baseline; the body predicted 17.5m.

Where the miss comes from: `test_reload.py` measured **18.6m** against 5.0m in the baseline, because the `slow_test` params the old `-m '(not slow_test)'` filter deselected now run — the DeepSeek-V3 debug variants and the quantized Qwen3 variants at tp=1, roughly 1.4–2.3m each (the tp=2 params skip instantly on one device). That is the cost of closing the hole the body describes, and it was unmeasurable before this build. The other never-run set, the four `sleep_mode` cases, cost 3.5m total, so index 3 landed at 11.5m.

Verdict: layout and routing validated; index 2 misses the 20m per-shard target. Proposed fix, same shard count: `reload` alone on index 2 (18.6m) and `params` + the three loader directories (5.5m) join index 3 (→ 17.0m). Slowest shard becomes 18.6m.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

_(Claude Code here, reviewing on @khluu's behalf.)_

The test moves and the ROCm fixes look good. The job layout needs another pass:
- Tensorizer is 21.3m. Move `test_tensorizer_entrypoint.py` (~3.7m) out, e.g. into Reload.
- `-m 'not slow_test'` got dropped, so ~11.6m of slow tests now run on every PR. Please put it back. Turning on slow tests should be its own PR.
- Core is a hand-picked list and already misses main's new `tests/model_executor/test_triton_dispatcher.py`. Make it a catch-all (`pytest model_executor --ignore=<what the other 3 jobs run>`) or move the root files into subdirs.
- The rebase isn't mechanical. #58607 added `mirror.amd.commands` to the old job, and a clean merge attaches them to the AMD Core mirror, so MI300 would rerun the whole suite. Each mirror needs its own commands (without the apt-get line).
- Intel marker in `models_distributed_intel.yaml`: it should be `-m "distributed(num_gpus=2)"` without the backslashes.

Then a fresh build, plus `/amd-ci run` for the test-amd.yaml changes.
